newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt to take 18 bln Ffr from CDC - paper.
newsitem.headline: French govt to take 18 bln Ffr from CDC - paper.

text.p: The French government is planning to take 18 billion francs from the reserves of state bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) in its 1997 budget, financial daily Les Echos said on Thursday.
The government takes money every year from the bank in return for a state guarantee on deposits if the bank were to collapse.
It took 23 billion francs in 1995 and around 21 billion in 1996.
Officials at the bank had no immediate comment while goverment officials were not available for comment.
But goverment sources have said it was likely that there would be a transfer from CDC reserves in the 1997 budget, which is due to be presented on September 18.
